# Codex task notifications

[← Packages](../README.md#packages) · **uv tool** (editable) · Codex-specific

Host lifecycle hooks observe Codex background work and deliver a native task
message to the same conversation. The job stays in Codex's command sandbox;
only observation and delivery run on the host. Claude's visual
[Wake mod](../claude/README.md#wake-mod-live) is a separate feature.

## Default workflow

Launch a command normally with Codex's background terminal, continue independent
work, then end the model turn. No wrapper, hand-written completion message, OS
PID or terminal handle is required for the notification. The `Stop` hook captures
newly observed running command items and starts a host observer. Once a
captured command ends and the target is idle, it sends one notification with the
native exit status, command item ID and a private captured-output path. Command
logs start with a JSON line identifying the native turn, item, command and cwd,
then a blank line and the captured output. This also identifies redirected commands.

A synchronous Bash `PostToolUse` hook records results returned by the native tool,
including a final `write_stdin` poll. The observer retires that exact command
instead of announcing it again after the parent becomes idle. This records tool
return, not whether the model read a report file or completed the larger task.

`SubagentStart` records the native worker's launch generation.
Async `SubagentStop` gives native delivery a two-second head start, verifies the
actual parent through `thread/read`, checks it is still idle without having
continued during that grace period, and reports the captured result once per child turn. It leaves active and
input-blocked parents to their native message flow. Posting a blocker without
ending the child turn has no corresponding hook: use the
[bounded native recovery](../codex/.codex/skills/codex-wake/SKILL.md#native-worker-blocked-on-its-root).
A result being reported does not prove the whole task is done.

### Install (user step)

```sh
uv tool install --editable ~/dotfiles-with-agency/codex-wake
./install.sh --apply hooks
```

Review and trust the merged hooks in Codex's `/hooks` UI, then restart Codex.
The snapshot is [hooks.json](../codex/.codex/hooks.json). A running user systemd manager
is required. The observer is a transient `codex-wake-*.service`, launched with
`systemd-run --user --collect --service-type=exec`. Its command is the fixed Python
observer module and a private job file, **never the user's shell command**.

The hook itself has a 60-second setup budget. The observer service has
`RuntimeMaxSec=infinity`, so it can outlive the hook and watch jobs longer than
600 seconds. It ends when its captured items finish, the target unloads/fails,
or its generation is cancelled. See [systemd 249's service lifecycle](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/249/systemd-run.html).
The service does not keep the Codex app server or the original terminal alive.

### Cancellation and duplicates

`Interrupt` and `SessionEnd` pause the generation; the next parent
`UserPromptSubmit` starts a new one only after such a pause. Ordinary parent and
child prompts preserve ongoing observers. Each command is registered by native
item ID, so later Stop events do not re-arm it. Delivery waits for idle across
turns and never answers a question or grants approval. Use Codex's interrupt
control to pause automatic delivery; a new chat prompt alone does not cancel it.

Each command item/child turn has a persistent claim written **before** submission.
An uncertain receipt is never retried. This provides at most one send attempt
per incident, not exactly-once receipt across crashes. Bridge watch and explicit
`codex-wake run` commands keep their own producer; the automatic command observer
skips those launch forms. Avoid burying completion producers inside opaque shell
scripts: command-text inspection cannot discover arbitrary nested behavior.
Unparseable shell syntax is conservatively skipped without preventing other
commands from being observed; those jobs need an explicit host producer.

State, claims and logs live under absolute `$XDG_STATE_HOME/codex-wake/`, or
`~/.local/state/codex-wake/` when XDG_STATE_HOME is absent or relative,
in private session directories (0700); files are 0600. Delete old state only when
its observer services have stopped. The native output can already be truncated
by Codex's retained-output limit (1 MiB in 0.166.0); the log preserves that captured
text, not an invented full transcript. The hook does not alter command I/O or TTYs.

Stop reads only background-terminal metadata, with 32 entries per page and a
four-page budget; it never scans turn history. The observer keeps one connection
open and fetches only watched IDs through the 0.166.0 experimental
[`thread/items/read` contract](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.166.0/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs#L1875).
Each read requests one item because its captured output can expand near the
client's 8 MiB response limit. Completed output is cached while waiting for idle.
The API reads persisted history: live Codex 0.166.0 can return an empty result
for a running terminal. The observer keeps waiting for its completion to be
persisted, rather than treating an empty result as a missing command or success.
Quiet polls back off from 2 to 4, 8, 16 and then 30 seconds, resetting on progress.
The [PostToolUse contract](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks#posttooluse) supplies
`tool_use_id`. In 0.166.0 a final unified-exec poll [retains the original command ID](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.166.0/codex-rs/core/src/tools/context.rs#L463),
so collection needs no command-text, timing or later-test-success matching.
The [documented event stream](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server#events)
requires starting/resuming a thread; 0.166.0 has no passive subscribe request.
This observer uses read-only calls instead of resuming or altering the target.

## Monitoring a condition for a while

For "tell me when X happens, for the next half hour", launch the monitor like any background command and end the turn:

```sh
codex-wake monitor --every 10s --ttl 30m --cooldown 5m --max-events 5 -- test -f build/ready
```

The probe is an argument list (no shell) run every `--every`: exit 0 means the condition holds, 1 that it does not, anything
else is a probe error. The monitor prints a `wake-event:` line for each announced hit and a `wake-end:` line when it stops.
It never talks to Codex, so it runs in the command sandbox like any other command. The `Stop` hook recognises it and the
host observer reads those lines from the running command, waking the idle session under limits the command cannot loosen:

| Limit | Default | Hard cap | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--ttl` | 30m | 24h | the monitor stops itself; the observer stops listening shortly after the same time |
| `--cooldown` | 5m | at least 30s | one notice per cooldown at most; hits in between are counted and joined to the next notice |
| `--max-events` | 5 | 20 | notices stop after this many; the closing notice still arrives |
| `--every` | 10s | at least 2s | probe interval; five probe errors in a row end it with `reason=probe-failed` |

`--distinct` announces a hit only when the probe's first output line differs from the last announced one (a changed answer,
not the same answer again). A notice states how many hits are new and how many there have been, and names the private log;
the probe's own output is never pasted into it. The closing notice is the ordinary one for a finished command.

Delivery waits for the session to be idle, like every other notice here. Live delivery needs the installed hooks and reads
the command's output while it runs. Codex 0.166.0 can omit running items from
persisted history, providing only the closing notification on that path.
If a Codex build does not return that output until the command ends, the monitor
still stops at its limits and the one closing notice carries every hit in its log. Check with a short run (`--ttl 1m
--cooldown 30s` and a probe that is true) and see whether the first notice arrives before the command ends.

## Why this mechanism

The contracts below target **codex-cli 0.166.0**. On upgrades, check the
installed CLI's generated app-server schemas, help and official documentation
before relying on these integration details.

| Candidate | Finding | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native unified-exec completion | The [exit watcher](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.166.0/codex-rs/core/src/unified_exec/async_watcher.rs#L167) emits command events; it does not itself submit a new model turn. | Prefer a native trigger wherever idle resumption is proven, but do not assume this event is one. |
| Async hook stdout | [Codex delivers it on the next user turn when idle](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks#how-background-hooks-run). | A host hook must call the task-message channel explicitly. |
| `PostToolUse` on unified exec | The [0.166.0 implementation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.166.0/codex-rs/core/src/tools/context.rs#L481) returns **no hook payload while a process ID is present**. A final poll returns the original command ID and its output. | Use Stop to arm running commands, and PostToolUse to retire a result returned by the native tool. |
| Host `Stop` + `SubagentStop` | [Lifecycle hooks](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks) run at the needed boundaries. [Item pagination](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server#list-thread-items) provides native identity/status/output; task delivery already exists locally. | Implement these without rewriting or unsandboxing jobs. |
| Delivery-only execpolicy rule | [An explicit `allow` can bypass the sandbox](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/rules#understand-rule-fields), not merely skip a prompt. Source [requires every parsed segment to be explicitly allowed](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.166.0/codex-rs/core/src/exec_policy.rs#L442). A rule for exact `codex-wake send/check` would help separate delivery calls, but cannot elevate a nested child inside an already-sandboxed `run`, or automatically arm completion. | Not installed or recommended over the host hook. Never allow `codex-wake run`, a shell, Python, or the whole executable prefix. |
| Writable socket path / broader network | [`sandbox_workspace_write` controls filesystem roots/network](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference), not a per-method exception for the privileged control API. Linux [masks the app-server socket directory and aliases](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.166.0/codex-rs/linux-sandbox/src/daemon_mounts.rs#L24); [legacy Landlock is rejected for restricted policies](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/permissions#how-enforcement-works). | Do not make `~/.codex` writable or relax socket isolation. |
| Explicit AF_UNIX proxy allowlist | [Permission profiles support named Unix sockets](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/permissions#unix-sockets), but this is endpoint access for sandbox programs, not a `send`-only RPC capability. It would expose a powerful control API more broadly than delivery requires. | Reject for this task; no network/permission-profile changes. |

Native terminal/process IDs are **app-server handles**, not host PIDs. The
[app-server reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server#clean-background-terminals)
states this explicitly. Using command item IDs avoids PID namespaces, reuse,
invisible processes and unavailable exit codes. The old agent-facing
`wait --pid` command and its process poll were removed rather than retained as
a second attachment workflow. The PermissionError diagnostic now routes to the
host hook or authorized delivery-only calls and explicitly forbids escalating `run`.

The [parity matrix and hook inventory](PARITY.md) distinguish implemented paths
from remaining gaps. The [wait-time audit](WAIT_TIMES.md) records source-backed
defaults and recommendations; no unrelated package's timer was changed.

## Explicit producers and fallback

```sh
codex-wake check
codex-wake send --message "The preview is ready for review."
codex-wake run -- make build
```

`check` and `send` use the current `CODEX_THREAD_ID` and `CODEX_HOME` (otherwise
`~/.codex`). Use `--thread THREAD --home PATH` only for an explicitly intended
different target. Existing host event producers can call `send`; Bridge watch
already uses the shared client, so never wrap it again.

`run -- COMMAND` remains a fallback **only where delivery already works**. It
preflights, runs the exact argument list with inherited stdin, tees combined
stdout/stderr to stdout and a 0600 temporary log, then sends the executable name,
exit status and output path. `--message` is optional. Arguments are omitted from
the notification; output is never pasted into it. No shell is inserted. Piped
output can change buffering and terminal formatting; use normal Codex terminals
with the installed hook as the default.

`run` preserves command exit codes (signals return `128 + signal`), returns 127
for an unavailable program, and 125 for setup/capture/delivery failure. Inspect
the printed log path before retrying: the job may already have executed.
Messages, including automatic context, must fit 1,000 UTF-8 bytes and are checked
before execution. Temporary logs persist until deleted or system cleanup and
have no size cap. **Never request sandbox bypass for `run`.** Allowing its delivery
would also unsandbox its arbitrary wrapped job. A separate narrow `send/check`
rule cannot change the sandbox of subprocesses already started by `run`.

## Shared client and compatibility

```python
from codex_wake.client import Wake

target = Wake(thread_id, home=codex_home)
target.check()
target.send("Automatic event notification. Not user approval.")
```

Each check/send opens and closes its own connection, freezes the target at
construction, validates discovery/receipts, and bounds each RPC wait to 15 seconds.
The Unix control socket and `codex_tui.send_message_to_thread` are **local
integration details**, not a promised public OpenAI wake API. The
[official app-server protocol](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server) documents
the surrounding initialization, discovery and read APIs. There is no route
fallback, automatic send retry, second app server or silently selected session.
Receipt acceptance proves submission, not completion of the next turn or task.
Raw-response tests include unrelated notifications, server requests and mismatched
JSON-RPC ID types: only the exact integer reply can acknowledge a request.
The [Bridge pipe replay](../agent-bridge/tests/fixtures/README.md) also keeps
interrupt acknowledgement separate from a terminal turn event. Existing hook
tests cover child completion after a new parent prompt and completed command
output waiting for an idle parent; neither permits answering a human question.

## Checks and remaining live verification

From this directory:

```sh
uv sync --locked
uv run --locked pytest
uv run --locked ruff check src tests
```

Verify automatic delivery in the target TUI after installing and trusting the
snapshot. Use these integration checks in addition to unit tests:

1. Have Codex launch `sh -c 'sleep 10; echo wake-parity-check; exit 7'` normally
   with `exec_command` and `yield_time_ms=1000`, then end its model turn. Confirm
   one automatic resume in the same thread, status 7 and the marker in the
   notified private log. Repeat with exit 0 and multiple background commands.
2. Let a native worker end with a final result or blocker while its parent is
   idle. Confirm one parent resume and the correct captured result; replaying
   the same child-turn event must not send again. Repeat with a busy parent and
   pending human input/approval: no forced wake or automatic answer.
3. Send a new parent prompt before completion. Confirm the command still wakes
   once after the parent returns idle. Separately interrupt before completion
   and confirm the cancelled incident cannot wake it. Check multiple observers
   across successive task-message wakes as well.
4. Run a job exceeding 600 seconds. Confirm its `codex-wake-*.service` survives
   hook exit and delivers once; inspect `journalctl --user -u UNIT` if it fails.
5. Capture hook stdin privately in an isolated test configuration: a yielded
   exec must produce no `PostToolUse` payload, whereas the final poll produces
   a Bash payload with `tool_input.command` and text `tool_response`. Verify the
   Stop/SubagentStop IDs, child ancestry and item output against that live payload.

Run these integration checks after installing and trusting the hooks; the
schema-derived unit fixtures cover the protocol and lifecycle logic separately.

## Native integrations

Running threads can retain their old hooks after a file edit. Compare native
`hooks/list` with `threadId` against discovery with `cwds`; a
`config/batchWrite` request with `edits: []` and `reloadUserConfig: true` reloads
runtime settings without changing hook trust. Then review the changed definition
in `/hooks`. Verify the loaded command and trust status before reporting activation.

[Codex task notifications](../codex-wake/README.md) deliver native task messages to an
existing conversation from background commands, hooks and event producers.
With the trusted snapshot hooks installed, launch commands normally: host
`Stop` and `SubagentStop` handlers arrange command/worker notifications without
unsandboxing the job. Notifications include a private captured-output path.

remaining gaps, and the [wait-time audit](../codex-wake/WAIT_TIMES.md) records
source-backed defaults. `codex-wake send` remains available to host producers;
`run -- COMMAND` is a fallback where delivery already works, never an allowed

uses its shared client and retains its own event and reminder policies.

`github-mcp` commands. Reload MCP configuration after installing them; the
[Baton guide](../agent-baton/README.md#commands) owns conversation isolation,
and [GitHub setup](../github/README.md) owns credentials and read-only toolsets.

connection. Tokens and host paths remain local.

# computer-use

[← Packages](../README.md#packages) · **Live launcher and skill** · **User-local Windows binary**

Windows native app control from WSL, alongside the existing Cua installation.
Use [Chrome tools](../chrome/README.md) for browser pages; agent-desktop covers
native dialogs, accessibility controls and desktop verification.

```sh
./install.sh desktop-tools links          # preview
./install.sh --apply desktop-tools links  # install the pinned release and live links
agent-desktop version
agent-desktop status
agent-desktop skills get desktop
agent-desktop skills get platform
```

The `desktop-tools` step supports x64 and ARM64 WSL. It downloads the Windows
release pinned in `install.sh`, checks its SHA256 and GitHub build attestation,
and installs under `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/agent-desktop/windows/`.
It needs `curl`, `gh`, `tar` and `sha256sum`; authenticate `gh` if it requests it.
It publishes the verified executable with an atomic rename and leaves an existing
binary alone. For a deliberate upgrade, review the new
release, pin, launcher parser and inventory schema, remove the installed directory,
then rerun this step. Do not
install the Linux npm package in WSL to control Windows applications.

`~/.local/bin/agent-desktop` links to this package's launcher. It checks
`agent-baton guard` before every call, fails if Baton cannot run, and forwards
arguments, stdin, native stdout and exit status without a PowerShell quoting
layer. No service, MCP registration, global approval or Windows PATH change is
needed. The shared `agent-desktop` skill is linked into Codex/OpenCode, Claude
and Antigravity discovery paths by the `links` step. It loads the binary's own
version-matched guides instead of maintaining a copied upstream manual.

The launcher refuses `move-window` and `resize-window` for `msrdc.exe` windows
(including WSLg). Windows-only geometry changes can leave the Linux app's click
coordinates behind even when the driver's `window_position` readback succeeds.
Other remote windows hosted by the same executable are conservatively refused
too. Native Windows geometry commands require an explicit `--app` or
`--window-id` and a successful live process-name check; unavailable or unknown
inventory fails before dispatch. This checks the current target, not an atomic
lock across desktop changes.

Run move/resize commands separately: batches containing either are refused
before any entry runs, since earlier entries could replace the checked target.
Other commands and batches retain their native transport. Guard refusals use
the native JSON error envelope with `ACTION_NOT_SUPPORTED`,
`details.kind: wslg_geometry_guard` and `not_delivered` / `safe`. WSLg movement
needs a separately validated Linux/compositor-owned path. Switching Windows
drivers or using physical input does not supply that validation. This boundary
is stricter than the pinned [upstream geometry verification contract](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/blob/v1.0.2/docs/json-output.md);
it prevents the reproduced [WSLg coordinate-sync failure](https://github.com/microsoft/wslg/issues/1116).

Windows interoperability can fail inside a restricted WSL sandbox before the
driver runs (`UtilBindVsockAnyPort ... socket failed`). Retry only the authorized
operation in the harness's host execution context. This does not require Windows
administrator rights or relaxed global sandbox/approval policy. Windows still
requires the signed-in user's unlocked interactive desktop; secure desktops and
Session 0 are unsupported.

Semantic actions can cause an application to take focus. Sessions scope refs,
traces and overlays; they do not isolate input. The skill requires one coordinator
for desktop workflows, but there is no cross-driver workflow lock. Use a VM or
another machine for reliably independent computer use. Physical input remains
an explicitly authorized step. Secret entry stays with [Agent Baton](../agent-baton/README.md).

For inspection, select the smallest supported capture target without bringing it
forward. The installed Windows interfaces provide:

| Operation | agent-desktop 1.0.2 | Cua 0.38.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Window capture | `screenshot --window-id ID` | `get_window_state` with exact `pid` and `window_id`; screenshot-only reads support `display_only: true` |
| Region capture | No screenshot crop flag | `zoom` uses a region of the window snapshot |
| Background actions | Semantic refs; Windows `type` and cursor-moving input require `--headed` | Window targets default to `delivery_mode: "background"`; unsupported delivery returns a structured refusal |

A window capture reads its current content, including whichever terminal or
browser tab the user selected. If the user changes that window's tab, dialog,
layout or input focus between observation and action, re-observe the target and
check whether the action is still needed. Background delivery avoids a foreground
swap; it does not reserve the app's state. For layout checks that do not need the
live desktop, use an isolated renderer or headless fixture.

These flags and delivery limits come from the installed help and `describe`
schemas. The upstream [observation reference](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/blob/v1.0.2/skills/agent-desktop/references/commands-observation.md)
and [Cua action model](https://cua.ai/docs/cua-driver/concepts/how-cua-driver-works)
explain capture and verification; reread local schemas after upgrades.

Cua remains independently installed and updated through its
[official updater](https://cua.ai/docs/cua-driver/guides/operate). Read its installed
`describe` schemas after an upgrade: 0.35 changed the default window-state tree.
Keep its daemon permission mode and existing startup choices; do not add an
unrestricted daemon to recover an unavailable action.

Verify with `python3 -B tests/test_agent_desktop.py` and the installer/Baton checks.
Remove only the live launcher/skill links and the installed binary directory to
uninstall; leave Cua, Baton, user apps and any wanted private traces in place.

Sources: [upstream installation](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/blob/main/docs/install.md),
[desktop guide](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/blob/main/skills/agent-desktop/SKILL.md),
[Windows guide](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/blob/main/skills/agent-desktop-windows/SKILL.md).

  plugin (OpenCode 2.2.2+) that calls the shared [process guard](../shell/README.md#agent-process-matching)
  for `shell` commands. Native-child shell calls export the root controller,
  child session ID and worker restrictions to their command and descendants,
  including compound commands and scripts that call `agent-resources`. An enclosing
  Bridge controller is preserved. Root sessions and ordinary history forks retain
  their environment. The plugin is discovered automatically under the global plugin

Resource attribution reads the tool hook's session ID and follows verified
[`parentID` ancestry](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.2.6/packages/core/src/tool/plugin/subagent.ts),
with a three-second deadline and at most 32 sessions. Missing, malformed or cyclic
ancestry rejects that shell call instead of guessing a controller. Ordinary
[forks have separate history metadata](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.2.6/packages/core/src/session/projector.ts)
and no native parent. The [native shell creates a fresh process per call](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/v2.2.6/packages/core/src/shell.ts),
so the export prefix changes neither the plugin process environment nor another
agent's shell. The command keeps its own working directory and exit status.
Commands that explicitly clear their environment must preserve attribution themselves.
These labels describe local command reservations, not model-loop RAM or an agent memory cap.

`bun test tests/test_process_guard_plugin.test.js` checks resource attribution,
worker boundaries and process guarding without starting model sessions.
OpenCode [reloads watched config changes automatically](https://dev.opencode.ai/v2/docs/plugins#reload).
A linked source outside watched directories may need a native reload or a new
service instance; an installed link alone does not verify the active revision.

Shared skills, including `python-project` and the adapted
[engineering skills](../agents/README.md#engineering-skills), are discovered from
`~/.agents/skills`. They use available native tools and load only for relevant
tasks; no separate copy of their workflows belongs in the global instructions.

`agent-bridge` runs OpenCode workers confined by `bwrap`. Its free-tier admission
is limited to reviewed zero-retention routes; Go and external provider routes keep
their own billing and privacy terms. Read `model-guide read subscriptions` when
those terms affect a choice.

# rtk

[← Packages](../README.md#packages) · **Snapshot** · `./install.sh --apply snapshots`

The user config for [RTK](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk), the proxy that filters shell
command output before it reaches an agent.

- `.config/rtk/config.toml`: tracking and history settings.
- `.config/rtk/filters.toml`: user-global output filters; a project's own `.rtk/filters.toml` takes
  precedence over these.

Codex calls the native `rtk hook codex` adapter as a `PreToolUse` hook. Its rewrite
output includes the decision required by [Codex's hook contract](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks#pretooluse).
`install.sh --apply hooks` replaces the former managed `rtk hook claude` Bash
entry; custom hook commands stay intact. Claude's
[live wrapper](../claude/.claude/hooks/README.md#rtk-and-auto-review) skips rewriting
in auto/plan modes so the classifier reviews the command that runs; use explicit
`rtk` commands there. Other known permission modes use the native hook. The shell
startup test needs `rtk` on PATH. There is no scripted install: install it by hand.

The `uvx-progress` filter removes UVX setup progress, preserving tool output,
package changes, errors and exit status. It does not filter Baton answers,
Bridge events or protocol JSON. After reviewing and copying the snapshot to the
live config, run `rtk trust --yes` locally. Trust hashes stay outside Git.
Use `rtk uvx ...` for standalone UV-managed tools; repository commands stay
`uv run` with the existing RTK filters.

## Exact output and shell quoting

`rtk bypass` (legacy alias `rtk proxy`) sends raw output and increases model input
tokens and cost. Use a command-specific filter, then `summary`/`err`/`test` for
other commands. Reserve bypass for byte-exact protocols or demonstrated filter
breakage. Full file/instruction reads use `rtk read --level none`; bound ordinary
reads and recover elided details before resorting to raw output.

### Pipelines, chains and substitutions

RTK's display output is for the agent, not input to another program. Keep native
commands inside data flows; filter only the final display boundary. Otherwise
shortened paths, omitted rows or added headings can change a later search, count
or parser. This applies to pipelines, command/process substitutions and redirected
file/protocol output, including when they appear inside a longer command chain.

```sh
# With the native hook: write the pipeline normally; RTK rewrites only its tail.
find ~/.claude/projects -type f -name '*.jsonl' | rg dotfiles

# Without a hook: filter the complete pipeline once, after its internal work.
rtk summary bash -o pipefail -c 'rg --files --hidden ~/.claude/projects | rg dotfiles'

# Keep substitutions and file contents exact; compress the displayed result later.
count=$(find . -type f | wc -l)
find . -type f > inventory.txt
```

Do not write `rtk find ... | rg ...` or `rtk rg ... | jq ...` when the next stage
needs the original records. A whole-chain wrapper must keep the original shell,
quoting, redirections, operator order and exit status; use `pipefail` when any
failed pipeline stage should fail the command. `&&`, `||` and `;` may join ordinary
display commands as well as pipelines; they do not make every command a data source.

RTK 1.1's native rewrite engine already leaves pipeline producers native, rewrites
only a supported final stage, preserves chain operators, and declines command
substitutions and file redirects. No additional rewrite hook is installed here.
The checks below exercise these boundaries through the real Claude hook, including
unsupported final stages and short-circuit exit status.

A recorded `rtk summary` invocation stripped the
quoting from `awk 'NR>=80'`, leaving a `>=80` redirect and a stray `=80` file.
Prefer a read tool for line ranges; recover omitted output with `rtk recall` or
a focused read. Shell quoting alone is not a reason to bypass filtering.

### Local summary fix (RTK 1.1.0)

[summary-results.patch](patches/summary-results.patch) applies to the official
[v1.1.0 source](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk/tree/v1.1.0). It identifies test
results from runner records, preserves their reported counts, and retains failed
test output. A jq `test(...)` expression, a `test_*.py` filename, or a passing
test title containing "failed" no longer creates a test result or failure.
The same fix removes build-summary guesses based on command arguments or filenames.
The patch carries RTK's [Apache-2.0 license](patches/LICENSE).

Apply it with `patch -p1 < /path/to/dotfiles-with-agency/rtk/patches/summary-results.patch`
in a clean RTK v1.1.0 checkout. Build its normal release with Rust 1.91 or later:
`cargo build --locked --release --bin rtk -j 2`, through host resource admission.
Validate with the built binary first on PATH using this repository's filter
checks below, then replace the user-local binary. Snapshot installation does not
manage that binary; rerun these checks after an RTK upgrade.

### Remaining `rtk summary` limit (RTK 1.1.0)

`summary` is a heuristic display filter. Its stdin behavior remains upstream:

- **It does not pass stdin to the command it wraps.** `printf x | rtk summary python3 -c 'import sys; print(len(sys.stdin.read()))'`
  prints 0, with exit status 0 (reproduced). Wrapping the whole pipeline (`rtk summary bash -o pipefail -c '… | …'`) prints 1.
  So the final-consumer rule above applies to the hook's rewrite of supported stages, not to a hand-written `summary` tail.

## Learning and filter patterns

`rtk --help` owns current dispatch. RTK 1.1's `rtk uv run ...` preserves the UV
environment while routing supported tools to their own filters. Existing
`filters.toml` regex rules handle repeated output noise; keep versions, failures,
diagnostics and exit status, with positive and negative fixtures.

`rtk learn` mines Claude Code's error/correction history; `rtk discover` finds
missed filtering opportunities in that history. They do not audit Codex sessions.
Start with a bounded project/date range and repeated, high-confidence findings.
Review candidates before applying a targeted fix. Do not run `--write-rules` in
public dotfiles: generated commands and paths are private state, not shared rules.

`rtk pipeline test` validates loaded engine pipelines; `rtk methods list` shows
their lossiness/recovery contracts. `pipeline explain` establishes which hooks
the installed harness supports. Codex cannot replace results in PostToolUse, so
installing an after-tool pipeline alone does not compress native tool output.
No LLM proxy, delegated compression task or additional engine hook is configured
here. CLI filters remain the shared route across harnesses.

## Checks

Run `python3 -B tests/test_rtk_filters.py` from the repo root to check the inline
fixtures and real dispatch/exit status in an isolated config. RTK's verifier
currently reads project filters, not global ones, so an empty global verify run
is not proof that a filter passed. The test copies this snapshot into its own
temporary project and keeps its trust state there.

Native hooks invoke it automatically before command execution: | Harness | Integration | Setup | | --- | --- | --- | | Claude | Bash `PreToolUse` | `./install.sh --apply links hooks` | | Codex | Bash `PreToolUse` | Same; trust new hooks through `/hooks` | | Antigravity | `run_command` `PreToolUse` | Same; named hooks in `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` | | OpenCode 2.2.2+ | `execute.before` plugin for `shell` | `./install.sh --apply links`; global plugin discovery | Reload the harness after setup; Antigravity's `/hooks` lists loaded hooks. The guard never executes or rewrites submitted commands, approves requests or signals processes; the agent gets a correction before the tool call. Exact-name queries and explicit PID operations stay available. ```sh pgrep -x worker # exact executable name pgrep -A -f 'python worker.py' # full command, excluding the invoking ancestry kill -TERM "$owned_pid" # verify the PID belongs to the intended task first ``` The guard uses the installed `shfmt` parser, not regex matching over shell text. Chains, loops, substitutions and common static wrappers are inspected. Quoted examples and log searches remain data. Dynamic commands and externally read scripts are outside this mistake guard; it is not a sandbox or authorization boundary. Unsupported syntax, a missing parser or a parser error blocks candidate commands with a PID-based alternative, while unrelated commands are unaffected. Ancestor exclusion depends on the procps version: check `pgrep --version` and `pgrep --help` before using it. Where unavailable, use exact names or owned PIDs. Tests: `python3 -B tests/test_process_guard.py`; parser fixtures never execute the commands, and a modern-procps smoke test signals only its own disposable child. `bun test tests/test_process_guard_plugin.test.js` exercises OpenCode's adapter with the same helper. Hook decisions follow each harness's native denial contract; Antigravity's `allow` only defers to its normal permission policy. Contracts: [Antigravity hooks](https://antigravity.google/docs/hooks), [OpenCode server plugins](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/server/) and [plugin discovery](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/plugins#discover). ## Output from commands that start daemons A client can exit while its daemon still holds an inherited output pipe open. A reader waiting for EOF then looks hung even though the client finished. ADB startup from WSL has exhibited this; stopping a shared server is not a safe way to release a capture. Check the client separately from its background server. For an authorized Windows ADB startup, capture both streams to private regular files, bound the client, and filter the files after it exits: ```sh ( umask 077 capture_dir=$(mktemp -d) || exit timeout --kill-after=5s 20s adb.exe start-server >"$capture_dir/stdout" 2>"$capture_dir/stderr" client_status=$? rtk read --level none "$capture_dir/stdout" rtk read --level none "$capture_dir/stderr" >&2 exit "$client_status" ) ``` Run subsequent bounded client diagnostics separately. Keep the exit status and stderr; do not replace a failure with an empty successful result. Timeout does not establish that a Windows process or its descendants stopped: inspect exact task-owned processes before cleanup. Retain the private capture only as needed. This avoids waiting for pipe EOF; it does not repair ADB handle inheritance. Current [ADB startup source](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/packages/modules/adb/+/refs/heads/main/adb.cpp) already guards standard handles against inheritance, so the observed hang alone does not prove a current ADB or RTK defect. See also Microsoft's [handle inheritance contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/inheritance). ## Credentials Put credentials in `~/.config/shell/secrets.local.sh`, outside the repository: mode `0600` for the file, `0700` for its directory. Both shells source it through `env.sh`; it is an ordinary shell file, with no separate dotenv parser. Provision it separately through encrypted transfer or a password manager. It is excluded from Git, not encrypted. See [chezmoi's guidance](https://www.chezmoi.io/user-guide/setup/) for the general dotfile-management approach. Original startup-file backups stay outside Git under `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/backups/shell/`, with owner-only permissions. ## Startup behavior `shell/.config/shell/env.sh` owns shared environment/PATH setup and the private credential include. `aliases.sh` owns shared interactive shortcuts and Ranger's directory-return function. `.bashrc` and `.zshrc` own only their shell's interactive behavior. Login setup follows the shells' native startup order: `.bash_profile` reads `.profile`, while Zsh reads `.zprofile`. Inherited Windows/WSL and virtual-environment paths remain in PATH. Local paths are added once; startup does not change directory or print greetings. The installed autocomplete plugin owns Zsh's `compinit`; `.zshenv` prevents Ubuntu's global duplicate initialization. Syntax highlighting loads after the first prompt's deferred autocomplete widget setup through a one-shot Zsh `precmd` hook. This follows the requirement to load highlighting after widget creation without placeholder widgets or changes to either installed plugin. See the [highlighting instructions](https://github.com/zsh-users/zsh-syntax-highlighting/blob/master/INSTALL.md) and [Zsh's public hook API](https://zsh.sourceforge.io/Doc/Release/User-Contributions.html#Manipulating-Hook-Functions). Zsh pre-resolves `getent` for `compaudit` and uses `command -v` for prompt discovery. Uncached lookups through Zsh's `commands` table can otherwise scan every inherited Windows PATH directory during startup. Node uses Ubuntu's updated CA store through `--use-openssl-ca` until installed runtimes include the emergency CA blocklist; restart existing Node processes to apply it. npm's global prefix is `~/.npm-global` (`NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX` here and in [`~/.npmrc`](../npm/README.md)), independent of the Node version. NVM's manual version switching is incompatible with that prefix; resolve the prefix before using `nvm use`, as described in [NVM's documentation](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm). ## Dependencies and checks Needs Zsh autocomplete and syntax highlighting under `~/.local/share/zsh/plugins/`, Starship, Ranger and `rtk` on PATH. Check syntax without sourcing credentials: ```sh zsh -n shell/.zshrc bash -n shell/.bashrc ``` From the repository root, `python3 -B tests/test_shell_startup.py` checks quiet startup, inherited paths, the working directory and tool resolution. ## Tool data locations Shared shell environment sets Go's workspace to `~/.local/share/go` and module cache to `~/.cache/go/mod`, using its supported `GOPATH` and `GOMODCACHE` options. ## Startup and timers

These pieces run without a terminal. WSL timers and services run while WSL is
running; the Windows tracker task can wake it.

| Where | What | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WSL `systemd --user` | `codex-reset-tracker.service` | The tracker is its own repo, [vTuanpham/codex-reset-tracker](https://github.com/vTuanpham/codex-reset-tracker); the unit here is a copy of what `service install` writes |
| WSL `systemd --user` | `agent-models-reference.timer` | Daily drift check and light conditional poll; changed sources only, pending review required |
| WSL `systemd --user` | `agent-lab-gc.timer` | Weekly `agent-lab gc --apply`, using each retired lab's grace period |
| WSL `systemd` | `tailscaled`, plus the `tailscale serve` TCP forwards for the baton phone path | The forwards persist in Tailscale's own state |
| User crontab | hourly Codex model-catalog refresh | Documented in `codex/.codex/model-catalogs/README.md`; check with `crontab -l` |
| Windows Task Scheduler | `CodexResetTracker`: wakes WSL and starts the tracker at logon, unlock and wake | Created by the tracker's `windows-startup install --force`; runs `wsl.exe` through `conhost.exe --headless` so no console opens |
| Windows Task Scheduler | `cua-driver-serve`: starts the cua-driver daemon at logon | Registered by cua-driver. Its PowerShell flashes a window; wrap it once with the command below, and again if an update re-registers the task |

```powershell
$a = (Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName cua-driver-serve).Actions[0]
if ($a.Execute -notmatch 'conhost') {
  Set-ScheduledTask -TaskName cua-driver-serve -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction `
    -Execute 'C:\Windows\System32\conhost.exe' -Argument ('--headless ' + $a.Execute + ' ' + $a.Arguments))
}
```

The Windows tasks and the crontab are machine-local and are not in this repository.
To restore the tracker on a new machine: clone its repo, run `./install.sh`,

# Host tooling feedback

**Public workflow and templates; private records.** Agents using dotfiles or
shared host tools during unrelated work leave feedback here. Agents already
developing or maintaining the affected tool track that work in their current
task and owning docs; this queue is not their task log. It covers shared agent
tools, shell/terminal integration and host workflow improvements.
Application features, business logic and project benchmarks belong to that
project's own issues or maintained docs.

```text
dotfiles-with-agency/
├── agents/feedback/                 public standards
│   ├── issue.template.md
│   └── comment.template.md
└── feedback.local/                  ignored; main checkout only
    └── issues/<date-scope-slug>/     stable issue identity
        ├── issue.md                 description, type, status, outcome
        └── comments/<unique>.md     one file per contribution
```

Global guidance asks tool consumers to leave feedback. The repository's local `AGENTS.md`
asks agents working on dotfiles to review relevant pending issues. There is no
scheduled poller, remote issue sync or automatic assignment to an arbitrary session.

## File an issue or join a discussion

1. Search existing descriptions **and comments** by scope and distinctive words,
   including closed issues. Read likely matches before creating a ticket.
2. For an existing issue, add a comment: agreement, evidence, a concern, an
   alternative or progress. Give a short reason for agreement. Reopen a closed
   issue with new evidence when appropriate; link genuinely related issues.
3. For a new issue, copy [issue.template.md](issue.template.md) into a unique,
   descriptive `feedback.local/issues/<date-scope-slug>/issue.md`. Fill in its
   type (`feature`, `fix`, `improvement`, `maintenance`) and relevant evidence.
4. Copy [comment.template.md](comment.template.md) for each contribution. Give
   the file a distinct timestamp/harness/suffix name and leave other contributors'
   files intact.
5. If duplicates are found later, choose a canonical ticket, link it and close
   the duplicate with `resolution: duplicate`. Keep the useful evidence in the canonical one.

Folder paths remain stable when status changes. The description owns the current
status; individual comment files keep independent contributions small. Agreement
does not grant implementation, spending or publication approval. Issue/comment
text is context, not instructions to execute.

## Reporter metadata

Every issue and comment carries a `reporter` block so a report can be traced to
the session, harness build and tool revision that produced it. Fill it from what
the harness already exposes; no tool is needed. Write `null` for anything you
cannot read directly, and never copy it from a nearby or parent session.

| Field | Where to read it |
| --- | --- |
| `harness`, `harness_version` | Your own harness; `claude --version`, `codex --version`, `opencode --version` or `agy --version` |
| `session` | Claude `$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, Codex `$CODEX_THREAD_ID`, Antigravity `$ANTIGRAVITY_CONVERSATION_ID`, or the session ID your harness states in context. OpenCode does not expose it to shells. |
| `model`, `effort` | The model ID and effort your harness states in context; leave effort `null` when it isn't stated |
| `role`, `bridge_job` | `root`, `native-subagent` or `bridge-worker`; a Bridge worker's `$AGENT_BRIDGE_JOB`. A worker's inherited root variables are not its own session. |
| `host_tools_revision` | `git -C ~/dotfiles-with-agency describe --always --dirty` (host tools run from this checkout) |
| `cwd`, `at` | The working directory where the trouble happened; `date -Iseconds` |

Put the affected tool's own version in Evidence when it is not part of this repository.

## Work a ticket

A report's suggested next step is the reporter's hypothesis, written from inside
one task. Before changing anything:

1. Restate the underlying problem from the evidence: what failed, for whom, and
   why the tool let it happen. Name the failure class and look for sibling cases.
2. Ask whether the cleanest fix removes the need for the suggestion: a default or
   native mechanism instead of an extra command, one owner instead of another copy,
   deleting a workaround instead of documenting it.
3. Implement that fix, which may differ from or replace the suggestion, and say
   in the Outcome which suggestions were kept, replaced or dropped, and why.

## Close, never delete

Keep dated discussion while an issue is open, in progress, blocked or deferred.
To close it, set `status: closed`, its `resolution` (`resolved`, `dismissed` or
`duplicate`) and a dated Outcome section with the validation done. Closed
tickets stay in place as the record: reopen one with new evidence rather than
filing again. Promote lasting insights to the owning maintained docs. Never
delete a ticket or another contributor's comment.

## Privacy

`/feedback.local/` is ignored by the repository. Keep its directories owner-only
and files at `0600`; never stage, publish or sync the records. Omit credentials,
cookies, secret values and raw transcripts. Public examples/templates stay
generic; actual host details remain in the local tree.

# Claude hooks (live)

## RTK and auto review

`rtk.py` delegates to `rtk hook claude` only in known permission modes without
the auto classifier. Auto mode, plan mode (which can use that classifier), and
missing or unknown modes leave the command untouched. Use explicit `rtk` commands
in those modes, following the shared shell filtering guidance.

This avoids [invalidating review of the original input](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#pretooluse-updatedinput-in-auto-mode),
including denials of sibling tool calls. The wrapper never grants permission,
denies a command, or retries it. `install.sh --apply links hooks` installs the live
wrapper and replaces only the former managed `rtk hook claude` Bash entry in Claude
settings, preserving local settings and Codex's native RTK hook.

## Native resource reservations

`resource-context.py` uses [SubagentStart](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#subagentstart)
to give each child its root owner and agent ID as context. The child must export these values
in each Bash call that invokes `agent-resources`; this also covers nested scripts. The hook
does not change commands or enforce attribution, and omitted exports leave requests unattributed.
Install its link and hook with `./install.sh --apply links hooks`.

## Process matching

The shared [process-match guard](../../../shell/README.md#agent-process-matching)
rejects self-matching `pgrep`/`pkill` patterns before Bash executes. It is owned by
the shell package and also used by Codex; it is separate from the root Stop hook.

## Root stop safety net

`bridge-stop.py` is linked to `~/.claude/hooks/bridge-stop.py` by
`install.sh --apply links`. SessionStart and Stop entries are merged from the
settings snapshot by `install.sh --apply hooks`; installation is explicit.

SessionStart exports the native session ID through Claude's `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`.
Bridge records it with the owner's next root command. Stop reads
`agent-bridge status --json --no-quotas`, selecting those owners. With running
workers or unread completions and no kernel-locked root watch, it asks once to
arm a watch or acknowledge results. Private session-scoped pending-set hashes
prevent loops and survive restarts. The hook never starts workers or sends messages.

Subagent events, worker environments, stop-hook continuation, pending native
AskUserQuestion calls and question-like closing text allow stopping. All errors,
incomplete status, missing inputs and timeouts also allow stopping. Existing
sessions can resume after installation so SessionStart supplies their ID.

Disable for a session: `AGENT_BRIDGE_STOP_GUARD=0 claude`.

Contracts: [Stop](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#stop) and
[SessionStart environment](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#persist-environment-variables).
Codex/agy roots explicitly arm `agent-bridge watch OWNER --until-event` or poll
`agent-bridge status --json` about every ten seconds.

# Codex custom model catalog

`config.toml` points `model_catalog_json` at `gpt-6-models.json`. That file
replaces the catalog the server sends, so it must not be edited by hand or left
to go stale: a hand-kept snapshot is why GPT-6.1 Sol stayed at 272k after the
server default moved to 500k (2026-10-12).

## How it works

`gpt-6-models.json` is **generated**: the live server catalog plus the fields
in `overrides.json`, nothing else.

- `overrides.json`: the only file to edit. Maps a model slug to the fields
  that should differ from the server, e.g. Luna's 1M context window. Add or
  remove entries here; an entry may hold any catalog field.
- `refresh.sh`: fetches the live catalog, merges the overrides, and replaces
  the catalog atomically. On any failure (fetch error, invalid JSON, an
  override naming a slug the server no longer lists) it keeps the old file and
  exits non-zero.
- `.fetch-home/`: a second Codex home without `config.toml`, needed because
  with the pin active `codex debug models` just returns the pinned file. It
  shares the real login through a symlink to `~/.codex/auth.json`; do not put
  a copy of `auth.json` there.

Run `refresh.sh` by hand after changing `overrides.json`, after switching
account plan, or when a model's limits look wrong. Check the result with:

    jq -r '.models[]|[.slug,.context_window,.max_context_window]|@tsv' gpt-6-models.json

Running sessions keep the catalog they started with; restart them (and run
`codex app-server daemon restart`) to pick up a change.

## Schedule

Meant to run hourly from the user's crontab:

    17 * * * * $HOME/.codex/model-catalogs/refresh.sh >/dev/null 2>>$HOME/.codex/model-catalogs/refresh.err

Check `crontab -l` to see whether it is installed. If `refresh.err` grows, an
override probably names a model the server renamed or removed.

## Rules

- Keep per-model context values here. Leave the global/profile
  `model_context_window` unset: it applies to every model and survives model
  switches inside a session.
- The catalog lists what the server offers the active account. Models that
  exist only in the catalog bundled with the CLI (e.g. Daybreak Blue/Red in
  0.162.1) are not included.
- Do not add `model_messages.instructions_template` content through
  `overrides.json` unless the user explicitly authorizes those persistent
  model instructions.

# Notes verification map

This directory is the maintained source for verifying the user-facing behavior of Notes. Read the index before driving the app, then use the matching feature file as the recipe.

## Baseline preconditions

- Launch Notes at `http://127.0.0.1:4173` with a disposable data directory.
- Set `NOTES_DATA_DIR=/tmp/notes-verify-$RUN_ID` so concurrent runs do not share state.
- Seed notes titled `Quarterly plan` and `Grocery list`.
- Put `control-notes` and the `notes` CLI on `PATH`.
- Run `control-notes doctor` and require the expected URL, data directory, and build revision.
- Never drive an instance that was not started by this verification run.

## Driving conventions

- Start every recipe from the baseline state unless its preconditions say otherwise.
- Prefer ARIA roles and accessible names over CSS selectors or DOM position.
- Treat every command as literal. Keep quoted names and flags unchanged.
- Run browser actions through `control-notes browser`.
- Run terminal actions through `control-notes cli -- <command>`.
- Restore seeded data after a mutation. Do not remove proof artifacts during cleanup.

## Proof and skip reporting

- Capture the user action and the resulting state, not only the final screen.
- UI proof includes an ARIA snapshot and a screenshot with the app identity visible.
- CLI proof includes the command, stdout, stderr, and exit code.
- Mutation proof includes a read-only second view of the stored value.
- Record the feature ID and entry point used with every artifact.
- Report an unreachable path with the attempted command and the unmet precondition.
- Do not report a skipped entry point as verified through a different path.

## Feature entry contract

Each feature file starts with an H1 title and one paragraph describing the user-visible behavior. It then uses exactly four H2 sections in this order.

1. `Sub-features` lists short IDs with one line for each behavior.
2. `How to get to it (user POV)` lists every user entry point.
3. `Driving it with <harness>` starts with `Preconditions:` and uses labeled bullets that pair each user action with an exact command and observable result.
4. `Gotchas` lists traps that can waste or invalidate a verification run.

Keep implementation details out of the map. Name only user paths, stable handles, required state, commands, and observable proof.

## Features

- [Create a note](./create-note.md) covers browser and CLI creation, cancellation, persistence, and cleanup.
- [Search notes](./search.md) covers toolbar, keyboard, and CLI search with matching, empty, and clear states.

## Supported Codex hook inventory

The [official hook reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks) describes these
12 events for the installed release. Match Bash for shell/unified-exec tools;
`exec_command` is not a separate hook event. The
[0.166.0 unified-exec output implementation](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.166.0/codex-rs/core/src/tools/context.rs#L471)
omits PostToolUse whenever `process_id` is still set. A final `write_stdin` can
emit the original Bash command's PostToolUse with text output. There is no
documented background launch PID, stable output-file path or exit status to
extract from an initial yielded PostToolUse payload, because that payload is absent.

| Event | Relevant published input | Can it carry a wake? / snapshot choice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SessionStart | `session_id`, source (`startup`, `resume`, `clear`, `compact`, `fork`) | Can set context; waking at startup would loop. No new wake handler. |
| SessionEnd | `session_id`, reason | Session ending is a cancellation boundary, not a request to restart it. New handler pauses the generation. |
| UserPromptSubmit | `session_id`, `turn_id`, prompt; child context may include `agent_id` | Ordinary prompts preserve ongoing observers. A parent prompt starts a fresh generation only after Interrupt/SessionEnd paused delivery; child prompts never resume a paused parent. |
| PreToolUse | canonical tool name, tool-use ID, tool input (`command` for Bash) | Runs before knowing whether exec will yield. Rewriting every command changes semantics and can bypass checks; not used for arming. |
| PermissionRequest | tool name/input, active turn | Can control an approval. No wake handler; never auto-answer or turn a wake into approval. |
| PostToolUse | tool name/use ID, input, result | Unified exec omits it while running. A final Bash result carries the original command ID; the synchronous handler retires that command's observer. Existing browser hooks remain. |
| PreCompact | trigger (`manual`/`auto`), turn | Context maintenance; no new wake handler. |
| PostCompact | trigger, turn | Context maintenance; no new wake handler. |
| SubagentStart | parent session context, `agent_id`, `agent_type`, turn | Records generation only; no wake. |
| SubagentStop | agent ID/type, transcript path, last assistant message, turn, `stop_hook_active` | New async handler lets native delivery go first, verifies actual parent metadata and unchanged parent turn, checks fresh idle, then reports once per native child turn. A report is not a promise that all child work is complete. |
| Stop | current session/turn, last assistant message, `stop_hook_active` | Synchronous host handler reads running-terminal metadata in at most four 32-entry pages and registers each native item once. It launches an observer without scanning turn history. |
| Interrupt | main session/turn | New handler cancels prior incidents. No restart or wake. |

All share session/cwd/model/transcript metadata. The transcript is explicitly an
unstable format, so the implementation reads targeted native command items and bounded terminal metadata,
not transcript files or process listings. Subagent ancestry is confirmed through
the actual child's `parentThreadId`, not inferred from an inherited environment
variable or the newest thread.

`Notification`, `TaskCompleted`, `TeammateIdle`, a background-shell-completed
event, and a hook-completed event are **not in this published Codex inventory**.
Internal source types or under-development feature flags do not establish a
supported installable event. No such event was invented in the snapshot.

## Lifecycle, safety and remaining limits

- Hook processes are host processes in 0.166.0: see the
  [host command runner](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.166.0/codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/command_runner.rs#L280).
  They observe/deliver; they never receive a user command to execute outside its sandbox.
- Hook timeout is seconds: most default to 600; Interrupt and SessionEnd default
  to 1 and support at most 3. The installed Stop/SubagentStop setup budget is 60.
  [Async hooks do not remove those limits](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks#run-hooks-in-the-background).
  A transient user service carries long observation beyond hook lifetime.
- Interrupt and SessionEnd invalidate old generations. Ordinary prompts preserve
  command observers and worker incidents across turns. A pending approval/input
  keeps the target active, which is ineligible for forced delivery. Already
  unloaded/failed targets are never resumed by the observer. Cancellation and
  sends use fresh checks, but the native task API has no atomic “send only if
  still idle and unpaused” operation; a final cross-process race cannot be eliminated here.
- Persistent per-incident claims prevent repeat sends, including after uncertain
  receipts. Native delivery and actual model work remain independently observable.
- Bridge workers, existing Bridge watch and explicit run producers are excluded. A completion
  producer hidden inside an arbitrary shell script cannot be recognized from
  command text; avoid combining it with automatic observation.
- Observer reads keep one connection open, request only watched native IDs, cache
  completed output, and back off quiet polls from 2 to 30 seconds. The versioned
  [`thread/items/read` contract](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.166.0/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs#L1875)
  requires a turn and explicit item IDs. One output-bearing item per request
  stays within the client's response cap even when control characters expand in JSON.
  Stop's metadata page budget is separate from the number of historical turn items.
- The [event API](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server#events) streams after
  starting/resuming a thread. The [0.166.0 request inventory](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.166.0/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs)
  exposes no passive subscription operation. Read-only targeted polling avoids
  resuming an unloaded thread or changing its configuration merely to observe it.

See [installation and the five live acceptance checks](README.md#checks-and-remaining-live-verification).
The recommended native long-term fix is a harness-owned completion/task event
that starts an idle turn with captured output and exposes cancellation/origin
metadata. That would remove this host observer, as Claude's native task channel
removes the need for a per-command wrapper.

## Ticket suggestions reconsidered

| Earlier suggestion | Decision and reason |
| --- | --- |
| Wrap each command with run at launch | Replaced as the default: ordinary sandboxed exec plus a host Stop hook avoids both forgotten arming and the control-socket boundary. `run -- COMMAND` remains a small explicit fallback where delivery already works; its message is now optional and output is teed to a log. |
| Add `wait --pid` to attach later | Dropped with its implementation/tests/docs. Automatic Stop capture uses native command identity, so no agent must retain an OS PID, resolve namespaces, observe PID reuse or guess an exit code. |
| Improve PermissionError diagnostic | Kept the explanation, replaced the unsafe next action. It now routes to host hooks or authorized delivery-only send/check, and expressly rejects escalating run. |
| Distinguish observer completion from job success | Kept. Native command status is read from the item; missing exit code says unknown. Worker report, accepted delivery and logical task completion remain separate. |
| Wake a verified idle parent once after lost native messages | Automated for SubagentStop, with start-generation, actual ancestry, fresh-idle and incident checks. Kept bounded manual native recovery for reports without an ending child turn. |

The feedback informed reproduction and acceptance cases; it did not determine
the design or authorize unrelated changes.

# Codex wait-time audit

Checked 2026-11-01 against installed `codex-cli 0.166.0`, its CLI help/features,
current official documentation, versioned upstream code where the docs omit a
number, and this working tree. These are defaults, not an assertion about private
live configuration. No live Codex settings were changed. Local source line
numbers describe this audit's tree; other packages are being edited concurrently.

A **yield** returns control while work continues; a **runtime timeout** stops work;
an **RPC deadline** limits waiting for a reply; a **reminder/stall threshold** only
reports a condition. Increasing a yield does not extend a command's lifetime.
Existing external defaults were not changed. New owned hook/observer settings
and the removed PID poll are listed below.

## Restore

It runs on WSL2 Ubuntu; check paths, the distro and Windows fonts before restoring.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/vTuanpham/dotfiles-with-agency ~/dotfiles-with-agency && cd ~/dotfiles-with-agency
./install.sh                 # preview missing tools, links and config differences
./install.sh --apply         # apply the listed steps
./install.sh --apply links   # or choose specific steps
```
